title: XXXVIII–XXXIX. How far the moral law is abrogated for believers
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): as toward ye rigor and mode belonging toward leading a human into obedience. — 4. — as toward sharpening sin into all concupiscence; — 3. — as toward curse and condemnation; — 2. — it stands as abrogated as toward ye first use belonging toward justifying; — For 1. — How far ye abrogation belonging toward ye moral law extends, and how far it obtains among ye faithful constituted under ye grace belonging toward Christ, stands as easily gathered from ye uses already set out. — XXXVIII. — But ye substance belonging toward ye obedience that ye law demands remains, even if ye mode and rigor belonging toward legal justification has ceased under ye Gospel. — XXXIX.
pass_b_english: XXXVIII. How far the abrogation of the moral law extends, and how far it obtains among the faithful constituted under the grace of Christ, is easily gathered from the uses already set out. For 1. it is abrogated as to the first use of justifying; 2. as to curse and condemnation; 3. as to sharpening sin into all concupiscence; 4. as to the rigor and mode of leading a human into obedience.
XXXIX. But the substance of the obedience that the law demands remains, even if the mode and rigor of legal justification has ceased under the Gospel.
source_text: XXXVIII. Abrogatio legis moralis quousque pertineat, & quousque obtineat inter fideles sub gratia Christi constitutos, ex usibus iam propositis facile colligitur. Nam 1. abrogata est quantum ad primum usum iustificandi; 2. quantum ad maledictionem & condemnationem; 3. quantum ad acuendum peccatum in omnem concupiscentiam; 4. quantum ad rigorem & modum ducendi hominem in obsequium. XXXIX. Obedientiae vero quam lex exigit substantia manet, etsi modus & rigor iustificationis legalis cessavit sub Evangelio.
